arxiv-2103-16199.title: Electronic properties of atomically coherent square PbSe nanocrystal superlattice resolved by STS
arxiv-2103-16199.creator: Daniel Vanmaekelbergh
arxiv-2103-16199.description: Abstract Rock-salt lead selenide nanocrystals can be used as building blocks for large scale square superlattices via two-dimensional assembly of nanocrystals at a liquid-air interface followed by oriented attachment. Here we report measurements of the local density of states of an atomically coherent superlattice with square geometry made from PbSe nanocrystals.

arxiv-2106-03325.title: Routing optimization on power packet dispatching system based on energy loss minimization
arxiv-2106-03325.creator: Shiu Mochiyama, Kazuhiro Koto, Takashi Hikihara
arxiv-2106-03325.description: Abstract Power packet dispatching system has been proposed for smart power management in the form of discretized packet. In this paper, we discuss the routing optimization of power packets on the network of power routers. We propose a cost metric for the power packet delivery by circuit analysis of the router network.

arxiv-2205-02494.title: Bott-Chern cohomology and the Hartogs extension theorem for pluriharmonic functions Thanks: The author was partially supported by NSFC grant 12001513, and NSF of Anhui Province grants 2008085QA18 and 2108085QA04.
arxiv-2205-02494.creator: Xieping Wang
arxiv-2205-02494.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xieping Wang. Let X X be a cohomologically ( n − 1 ) (n-1) -complete complex manifold of dimension n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 . We prove a vanishing result for the Bott-Chern cohomology group of type ( 1 , 1 ) (1,1) with compact support in X X , which combined with the well-known technique of Ehrenpreis implies a Hartogs type extension theorem for pluriharmonic functions on X X . 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification

arxiv-2212-01305.title: Energetic requirements of the gamma-ray emission from pulsars: A nonparametric analysis of the data in the Fermi-LAT 12-Year Catalog 2022 Energetic requirements of the gamma-ray emission from pulsars: A nonparametric analysis of the data in the Fermi-LAT 12-Year Catalog – References
arxiv-2212-01305.creator: Houshang Ardavan
arxiv-2212-01305.description: Abstract The prevalent view that the radio-loud gamma-ray pulsars have gamma-ray luminosities that exceed their radio luminosities by several orders of magnitude is based on the assumption that the decay with distance of their gamma-ray fluxes obeys the inverse-square law as does that of their radio fluxes.

arxiv-2212-06591.title: Bubble nucleation and gravitational wave from holography
arxiv-2212-06591.creator: Yidian Chen, Danning Li, Mei Huang
arxiv-2212-06591.description: Abstract We investigate the bounce solution in the holographic QCD and electroweak models with first-order phase transition. The strength parameter α \alpha , inverse duration time β / H \beta/H and bubble wall velocity v w v_{w} in the gravitational wave power spectra are calculated by holographic bounce solution.

arxiv-2301-10544.title: Stray field computation by inverted finite elements: a new method in micromagnetic simulations
arxiv-2301-10544.creator: Tahar Z. BOULMEZAOUD 1,2,3, Keltoum KALICHE 1,3
arxiv-2301-10544.description: Abstract . In this paper, we propose a new method for computing the stray-field and the corresponding energy for a given magnetization configuration. Our approach is based on the use of inverted finite elements and does not need any truncation. After analyzing the problem in an appropriate functional framework, we describe the method and we prove its convergence.

arxiv-2303-03890.title: Improved Superscaling in Quasielastic Electron Scattering with Relativistic Effective Mass
arxiv-2303-03890.creator: P.R. Casale, J.E. Amaro, V.L. Martinez-Consentino, I. Ruiz Simo
arxiv-2303-03890.description: Abstract Superscaling in electron scattering from nuclei is re-examined paying special attention to the definition of the averaged single-nucleon responses. The validity of the extrapolation of nucleon responses in the Fermi gas has been examined, which previously lacked a theoretical foundation.

arxiv-2309-13750.title: Tests of subgrid models for star formation using simulations of isolated disk galaxies 2021 Tests of subgrid models for star formation using simulations of isolated disk galaxies – 20
arxiv-2309-13750.creator: Folkert S. J. Nobels, Joop Schaye, Matthieu Schaller, Sylvia Ploeckinger, Evgenii Chaikin, and Alexander J. Richings
arxiv-2309-13750.description: Abstract We use smoothed-particle hydrodynamics simulations of isolated Milky Way-mass disk galaxies that include cold, interstellar gas to test subgrid prescriptions for star formation (SF). Our fiducial model combines a Schmidt law with a gravitational instability criterion, but we also test density thresholds and temperature ceilings.

arxiv-2310-13868.title: Symmetry-dependent dielectric screening of optical phonons in monolayer graphene
arxiv-2310-13868.creator: Loïc Moczko, Sven Reichardt, Aditya Singh, Xin Zhang, Luis E. Parra López, Joanna L. P. Wolff, Aditi Raman Moghe, Etienne Lorchat, Rajendra Singh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Hicham Majjad, Michelangelo Romeo, Arnaud Gloppe, Ludger Wirtz, Stéphane Berciaud
arxiv-2310-13868.description: Abstract Quantised lattice vibrations ( i.e. , phonons) in solids are robust and unambiguous fingerprints of crystal structures and of their symmetry properties. In metals and semimetals, strong electron-phonon coupling may lead to so-called Kohn anomalies in the phonon dispersion, providing an image of the Fermi surface in a non-electronic observable.

arxiv-2404-08200.title: Fully quantum arbitrarily varying channel coding for entanglement-assisted communication
arxiv-2404-08200.creator: Paula Belzig
arxiv-2404-08200.description: Abstract If a sender and a receiver lack precise knowledge about the communication line that connects them, designing a scheme to reliably transmit information becomes more challenging. This has been studied in classical and quantum information theory in the context of compound channel models and arbitrarily varying channel models.

arxiv-2405-16383.title: Rewarded Region Replay (R3) for Policy Learning with Discrete Action Space
arxiv-2405-16383.creator: Bangzheng LiMIT liben@mit.edu Ningshan MaMIT ningshan@mit.edu Zifan WangMIT atticusw@mit.edu
arxiv-2405-16383.description: Abstract We introduce a new on-policy algorithm called Rewarded Region Replay (R3), which significantly improves on PPO in solving environments with discrete action spaces. R3 improves sample efficiency by using a replay buffer which contains past successful trajectories with reward above a certain threshold, which are used to update a PPO agent with importance sampling.

arxiv-2406-09111.title: Optimal demonstration of generalized quantum contextuality
arxiv-2406-09111.creator: Soumyabrata Hazra, Debashis Saha, Anubhav Chaturvedi, Subhankar Bera, A. S. Majumdar
arxiv-2406-09111.description: Abstract Finding a set of empirical criteria fulfilled by any theory that satisfies the generalized notion of noncontextuality is a challenging task of both operational and foundational importance. The conventional approach of deriving facet inequalities from the relevant noncontextual polytope is computationally demanding.

arxiv-2410-16451.title: Susu Box or Piggy Bank: Assessing Cultural Commonsense Knowledge between Ghana and the U.S.
arxiv-2410-16451.creator: Christabel Acquaye Haozhe An Rachel Rudinger
arxiv-2410-16451.description: Abstract Recent work has highlighted the culturally-contingent nature of commonsense knowledge Shen et al. (2024) . We introduce AMAMMER ε ( \textipa /A:.mA:.mu:.reI/), from the Akan word meaning ‘culture.’ This test set of 525 multiple-choice questions is designed to evaluate the commonsense knowledge of English LLMs, relative to the cultural contexts of Ghana and the United States.

arxiv-2411-00039.title: Linear Chain Transformation: Expanding Optimization Dynamics for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
arxiv-2411-00039.creator: Yulong Wang, Chang Zuo, Yin Xuan, Hong Li, Ni Wei
arxiv-2411-00039.description: Abstract Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) has become essential for adapting pretrained models to specific downstream tasks. In this paper, we propose Linear Chain Transformation (LinChain) , a novel approach that introduces a sequence of linear transformations during fine-tuning to enrich optimization dynamics.

arxiv-2502-20168.title: Accelerating Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with State-Space World Models
arxiv-2502-20168.creator: Maria Krinner 1 , Elie Aljalbout 1 , Angel Romero, Davide Scaramuzza
arxiv-2502-20168.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful approach for robot learning. However, model-free RL (MFRL) requires a large number of environment interactions to learn successful control policies. This is due to the noisy RL training updates and the complexity of robotic systems, which typically involve highly non-linear dynamics and noisy sensor signals.

britannica-1911-suez-canal.title: Suez Canal (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-suez-canal.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-suez-canal.description: Article 'Suez Canal' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. there was no direct water communication between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, but at various eras such communication existed by way of the Nile.

plos-pone-0002426.title: In Vivo -to- In Silico Iterations to Investigate Aeroallergen-Host Interactions
plos-pone-0002426.creator: Alba Llop-Guevara, Marc Colangelo, Derek K. Chu et al.
plos-pone-0002426.description: PLOS ONE research article. Allergic asthma is a complex process arising out of the interaction between the immune system and aeroallergens. Yet, the relationship between aeroallergen exposure, allergic sensitization and disease remains unclear. This knowledge is essential to gain further insight into the o

pmc-10477314.title: Modelling the potential of forest management to mitigate climate change in Eastern Canadian forests
pmc-10477314.creator: Abderrahmane Ameray, Yves Bergeron, Xavier Cavard
pmc-10477314.description: Climate change poses a serious risk to sustainable forest management, particularly in boreal forests where natural disturbances have been projected to become more severe. In three Quebec boreal forest management units, biomass carbon storage under various climate change and management scenarios was projected over 300 years (2010–2310) with a process-based dynamic landscape model (PnET-succession for Landis-II).

pmc-10738325.title: HEALTHY AGING AND OLDER ADULTS WITH AUTISM: A SCOPING REVIEW
pmc-10738325.creator: Mary Stringfellow, Noelle Fields, Kathy Lee, Keith Anderson
pmc-10738325.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong diagnosis. While several studies have examined the effects of this disorder throughout childhood, few have considered older adulthood and the differences between allistic (i.e., persons who are not affected by autism) and autistic older adults.

pmc-11409808.title: Genetically predicted dietary intake and risks of colorectal cancer: a Mendelian randomisation study
pmc-11409808.creator: Tung Hoang, Sooyoung Cho, Ji-Yeob Choi, Daehee Kang, Aesun Shin
pmc-11409808.description: BackgroundEffects of confounders on associations between diet and colorectal cancer (CRC) in observational studies can be minimized in Mendelian randomization (MR) approach. This study aimed to investigate observational and genetically predicted associations between dietary intake and CRC using one-sample MR.

pmc-11431560.title: Potential Skin Health Benefits of Abalone By-Products Suggested by Their Effects on MAPKS and PI3K/AKT/NF-kB Signaling Pathways in HDF and HaCaT Cells
pmc-11431560.creator: Eun-A Kim, Nalae Kang, Jun-Ho Heo, Areumi Park, Seong-Yeong Heo, Chang-Ik Ko, Yong-Seok Ahn, Ginnae Ahn, Soo-Jin Heo
pmc-11431560.description: Abalone, a marine edible gastropod with nutritional value, is a popular seafood delicacy worldwide, especially in Asia; however, viscera by-products are generally discarded during processing. Therefore, we investigated the skin health benefits of abalone viscera ultrasonic extract (AVU) in human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs) and human keratinocyte (HaCaT) cells.

pmc-11663925.title: Comparative evaluation of negative lymph node count, positive lymph node count, and lymph node ratio in prognostication of survival following completely resection for non-small cell lung cancer: a multicenter population-based analysis
pmc-11663925.creator: Qiming Huang, Shai Chen, Yuanyuan Xiao, Wei Chen, Shancheng He, Baochang Xie, Wenqi Zhao, Yuhui Xu, Guiping Luo
pmc-11663925.description: ObjectiveLung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Lymph node involvement remains a crucial prognostic factor in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and the TNM system is the current standard for staging. However, it mainly considers the anatomical location of lymph nodes, neglecting the significance of node count.

pmc-11688368.title: Neurochallenges in smart cities: state-of-the-art, perspectives, and research directions
pmc-11688368.creator: Begüm Özkaynak, Necati Aras, İrem Daloğlu Çetinkaya, Cem Ersoy, Özlem Durmaz İncel, Mutlu Koca, İrem Nalça, Turgut Tüzün Onay, Sinan Öncü, Berivan Ülger Vatansever, Eda Yücesoy, Can A. Yücesoy
pmc-11688368.description: Smart city development is a complex, transdisciplinary challenge that requires adaptive resource use and context-aware decision-making practices to enhance human functionality and capabilities while respecting societal and environmental rights, and ethics. There is an urgent need for action in cities, particularly to (i) enhance the health and wellbeing of urban residents while ensuring inclusivity in urban development (e.g.

pmc-11757910.title: scMMAE: masked cross-attention network for single-cell multimodal omics fusion to enhance unimodal omics
pmc-11757910.creator: Dian Meng, Yu Feng, Kaishen Yuan, Zitong Yu, Qin Cao, Lixin Cheng, Xubin Zheng
pmc-11757910.description: Multimodal omics provide deeper insight into the biological processes and cellular functions, especially transcriptomics and proteomics. Computational methods have been proposed for the integration of single-cell multimodal omics of transcriptomics and proteomics. However, existing methods primarily concentrate on the alignment of different omics, overlooking the unique information inherent in each omics type.

pmc-12656085.title: Automated EMG-Based Classification of Upper Extremity Motor Impairment Levels in Subacute Stroke
pmc-12656085.creator: Alexey Anastasiev, Hideki Kadone, Aiki Marushima, Hiroki Watanabe, Alexander Zaboronok, Shinya Watanabe, Akira Matsumura, Kenji Suzuki, Yuji Matsumaru, Hiroyuki Nishiyama, Eiichi Ishikawa, Yehuda Weizman
pmc-12656085.description: Rehabilitation of upper extremity (UE) impairments after stroke requires regular evaluation, with standard methods typically being time–consuming and relying heavily on manual assessment by therapists. In our study, we propose automating these assessments using electromyography (EMG) as a core indicator of muscle activity, correlating passive and active EMG signals with clinical motor impairment scores.

pmc-12749921.title: The association between internal and external measures of training load in elite rowers during ergometer training
pmc-12749921.creator: Xinyu Dai, Jihong Yan, Xuecui Bi
pmc-12749921.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). While traditional rowing metrics such as stroke rate and split times offer basic performance feedback, they do not fully reflect individual physiological responses, and the relationship between external and internal training loads remains inadequately characterized in rowing ergometer training. This study systematically investigated the correlations between two key internal load measures—training impulse (TRIMP) and session rating of perceived exertion training load (sRPETL)—and three biomechanical external load indicators in elite rowers, with the aim of establishing a more comprehensive training monitoring framework.

pmc-13132528.title: Robotic total gastrectomy: Key operative maneuvers and optimal use of the fourth arm
pmc-13132528.creator: Anneliese N Hierl, Brian D Badgwell, Paul F Mansfield, Naruhiko Ikoma
pmc-13132528.description: Background:The robotic platform offers distinct advantages for total gastrectomy, particularly through effective use of the fourth robotic arm.1 When used deliberately, the fourth arm enables stable counter-traction, single-surgeon control, and creation of a consistent surgical workspace, facilitating precise dissection and safe reconstruction.2Methods:We present a video of robotic total gastrectomy performed for a patient with gastric adenocarcinoma.

pmc-13250987.title: In Situ Observation of Radiation Damage in Rhabdophane- and Churchite-Type Rare-Earth Phosphate Nanocrystals
pmc-13250987.creator: Mohamed Ruwaid Rafiuddin, Anamul Haq Mir, Yingjie Zhang
pmc-13250987.description: Rhabdophane (REPO4·H2O; RE = La to Dy) and churchite (RE′PO4·2H2O; RE′ = Gd to Lu and Y) are secondary minerals formed via hydrothermal alteration of primary rare-earth minerals such as monazite (REPO4; RE = La to Gd) and xenotime (RE′PO4; RE′ = Tb to Lu and Y). Monazite and xenotime are promising host matrices for actinide-rich nuclear wastes.

pmc-13356142.title: Cationic carbon dot–silver nanohybrids with enhanced stability and redox control
pmc-13356142.creator: Nicolás Santos, Javier Muñoz, Marco Soto-Arriaza, Carlos Jara-Gutiérrez, Joan Villena, Manuel Ahumada
pmc-13356142.description: Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) show promise for biomedical applications, but their functional stability remains a major challenge. Here, the photochemical synthesis of hybrid AgNPs using carbon dots (CDs) as both reducing and capping agents (CDs–AgNPs) is described, producing highly stable nanostructures under physiological conditions.

pmc-13520329.title: Comparison of the efficacy of the oXiris filter and the ST-100 filter in patients with postoperative cardiac surgery infections combined with acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13520329.creator: Rui Wang, Yucheng Ren, Yunlin Song, Ying Li, Bingyu Ma, Yaowei Tong, Wangtao Zhou
pmc-13520329.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveComparison of the efficacy of the oXiris filter and the ST-100 filter in patients with postoperative cardiac surgery infections combined with acute kidney injury.MethodsThis is a retrospective cohort study of patients with postoperative cardiac surgical infections combined with acute kidney injury who underwent continuous renal replacement therapy from January 2023 to April 2024 in the Critical Care Medicine Centre of the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University.

pmc-13559813.title: Educational Case: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST)
pmc-13559813.creator: Simmi Patel, Rana Naous
pmc-13559813.description: ctives for all three competencies, see https://doi.org/10.1016/j.acpath.2023.100086.1 The following fictional case is intended as a learning tool within the Pathology Competencies for Medical Education (PCME), a set of national standards for teaching pathology. These are divided into three basic competencies: Disease Mechanisms and Processes, Organ System Pathology, and Diagnostic Medicine and Therapeutic Pathology.

pmc-13636095.title: Exploring immune dysfunction in bronchiectasis: a focus on natural killer cells using single-cell transcriptomes
pmc-13636095.creator: Bumhee Yang, Dongjun Kim, Geonhui Min, InSook Jeon, Eung-Gook Kim, Hyun Je Kim, Hyun Lee
pmc-13636095.description: ExtractBronchiectasis is characterised by persistent airway inflammation, impaired mucociliary clearance and recurrent respiratory infection [1]. Despite its increasing prevalence and clinical burden, the systemic immune mechanisms contributing to disease progression remain poorly understood [1, 2]. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) have revolutionised our understanding of cellular heterogeneity and immune dysregulation in chronic respiratory diseases, including bronchiectasis [3–5].

uslaw-usc-t22-s5464.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 63 (Support For East European Democracy (Seed)); Subchapter V (Additional Seed Program Actions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
